messages:
Tess (CSM): Quick sync — Rowan reported a provisioning knot during private deploy. Network routes aren't converging and KMS calls intermittently return AccessDenied. Not a full outage but this is a Week1 friction that could become a renewal signal if not smoothed. Who can triage?
Arjun (NetEng): I can take network. I pulled the tunnel config and customer didn't advertise 10.0.1.0/24 on their side; we see traffic blackholed. Also BGP sessions are flapping on one peer.
Clara (Security): For KMS I saw AccessDenied on GetKeyRotationStatus — likely the customer IAM role doesn't include kms:DescribeKey or kms:Decrypt on the CMK ARN. If they used our example policy it should be fine but variants often omit the decrypt bit.
Tess (CSM): Rowan just posted their role ARN in the ticket: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rowan-redwood-deploy. Can y'all simulate? I'll ask them to keep the window open for a live call.
Nate (Onboard): Running the validation suite now against their staging sim: `./priv-deploy-validate --target=rowan-staging --checks network,kms,logs` — will paste failures.
DeployBot: validation job queued #4821 — status: running.
Nate (Onboard): results: network-check FAIL -> missing route 10.0.1.0/24; bgp: neighbor 10.10.10.2 state: Active -> flapping. kms-check FAIL -> AccessDenied for kms:DescribeKey on arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01. audit-logs-check PASS.
Arjun (NetEng): I'll DM RowanNet (their network lead) to request they advertise the prefix and check BGP timers. Recommend adding static route fallback on their firewall for the prod subnet until BGP stabilizes. I can provide the exact commands for Forti/ASA.
Clara (Security): Draft policy snippet for their role — minimal permissions to meet onboarding (they should scope to the key ARN):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01"
    }
  ]
}
```
Use that and request they attach it to the deploy role. Also confirm there are no deny statements in their org SCP.
Tess (CSM): Nice. Action items so we have a single source: 1) Arjun -> request prefix advertisement + static route fallback (ETA 10m) 2) Clara -> send policy snippet to Rowan CISO + check for org-level denies (ETA 30m) 3) Nate -> re-run validation after changes and paste green runbook snippet (ETA after fixes) 4) Tess -> flag renewal risk in CRM if Week1 unresolved in 72h and schedule retro. Who owns the 72h watch?
Arjun (NetEng): I can own the 72h watch for network. I'll follow up on cloud provider ticket if BGP keeps flapping.
Nate (Onboard): After fixes I'll push a small runbook addition: `if bgp_flapping then add_static_route && monitor 1h` and attach to the customer onboarding doc.
Tess (CSM): I'll capture this feedback in the onboarding retro doc and request a short postmortem with Rowan after cutover. Link: http://redwood.internal/onboard/rowan-retro (internal). 
Clara (Security): One more ask — ask the customer to run `aws sts get-caller-identity` from their deploy environment and paste output so we can mirror the ARN in our sim. Avoid sharing tokens obviously.
Rowan (external): thanks — our infra lead applied the policy and added a static route. We'll stand by for your re-run. :thumbsup:
Nate (Onboard): re-run results: all checks PASS. BGP stabilized after timer tweak, KMS calls now succeed. I'll upload the validation log to the runbook and mark this step as automated in future runs.
Tess (CSM): Great job team. I'll mark this resolved in the ticket and keep the renewal watch open for 72h but will note the positive outcome in CRM. Capture any small UX asks for our docs (Arjun/Clara/Nate, please add short notes). :party_parrot:
